questions.prompt: Why are plants grown from cuttings identical to the parent?
options: They come from only one parent, with no mixing of features
They are watered the same way
They are grown in the same soil
They grow at the same time

questions.prompt: In the Propagation Lab, planting a potato leaf failed but a piece of potato with an eye grew. What does this show?
options: New potato plants grow from buds (eyes) on the tuber

questions.prompt: What are the ADVANTAGES of vegetative propagation for farmers? Choose all that apply.
options: Plants grow faster than from seed
Good features (like sweet fruit) are kept exactly
Plants that don't make good seeds can still be grown
questions.explain: Identical plants are useful, but also risky.

questions.prompt: Most bananas grown for sale are propagated vegetatively, so the plants are genetically identical. Explain one benefit and one serious risk of this.
questions.modelAnswer: Benefit: every plant has the same good features, such as sweet, seedless fruit, and they grow reliably and quickly. Risk: because all plants are identical, a disease that can attack one can attack them all; a single new fungus or virus could wipe out whole plantations, since there is no variety to give some plants resistance.
rubric: The risk of disease spreading through identical plants
questions.explain: Criterion D: evaluate a farming practice.

questions.text: Reproduction involving only one parent is called ___ reproduction.
questions.explain: The offspring are identical to the parent.

questions.prompt: Where are the ‘eyes’ on a potato?
questions.explain: The potato is a swollen underground stem.
